sources.summary: SDK maintainer (bergundy): 'if a handler isn't registered at the time a signal is received by the SDK, it is buffered in memory.' Recommends setDefaultSignalHandler as catch-all for visibility.

sources.label: Temporal docs — Errors: Unhandled Command + Pending Signals Limit Exceeded
sources.summary: UnhandledCommand = WFT failed because workflow attempted to close itself without handling new Events that arrived since WFT start. Transient; a retry WFT is scheduled. Pending Signals Limit Exceeded = workflow reached capacity for pending signals (server-side buffer cap).

sources.label: Temporal API proto — WorkflowTaskFailedCause enum
sources.summary: UNHANDLED_COMMAND=1: 'Between starting and completing the workflow task (with a workflow completion command), some new command (like a signal) was processed into workflow history. The outstanding task will be failed with this reason, and a worker must pick up a new task.' PENDING_SIGNALS_LIMIT_EXCEEDED=28: server-side signal buffer cap.

sources.label: Temporal community: Continuously signalWithStart behaviour (maxim)
sources.summary: Temporal maintainer (maxim): on race between completion and a new signal, server fails the last WFT with UnhandledCommand and rolls back so the signal is processed. If the signal arrives after the workflow completed at the service, a new execution is started (signalWithStart). 'signals cannot be lost if the workflow code is written correctly' — conditional on a handler existing.

sources.label: Temporal community: What happens to signals sent to a closing workflow
sources.summary: Drain signal channel before exit; Temporal rolls back to last blocked state to give the workflow a chance to handle a signal arriving during the close window.

sources.label: Temporal community: Async drain signal & Unhandled Command (maxim)
sources.summary: 'There is no way to eliminate UnhandledCommand as it is not an error but an indication of the race condition between workflow completion and new signals.' Benign when channel is drained correctly.

sources.label: TS SDK workflow-client.ts — query() routes to a worker that replays history
sources.summary: query() uses QueryWorkflow RPC; signal() resolves on server acceptance (does not wait for processing). QueryRejectedError thrown when queryRejectCondition rejects (e.g. workflow not open).

sources.label: TS SDK interfaces.ts — query handlers are live read-only ops
sources.summary: isReplayingHistoryEvents returns false during query handlers and update validators — 'live read-only operations that should not be considered as replaying history events.' Confirms queries execute on a live poller, not from stored history.

sources.label: Temporal docs — Handling Signals, Queries, & Updates
sources.summary: Workflow execution is single-threaded; handlers run interleaved with main workflow. 'finish running all handlers before the Workflow run completes' via all_handlers_finished. Handler Unfinished Policy controls warnings for in-flight handlers.

sources.label: TS SDK common/workflow-options.ts — WorkflowIdReusePolicy + WorkflowIdConflictPolicy
sources.summary: ALLOW_DUPLICATE is default ReusePolicy (start allowed if previous is Closed). ConflictPolicy: FAIL / USE_EXISTING / TERMINATE_EXISTING for a RUNNING workflow with same ID.

sources.label: TS SDK common/failure.ts — WorkflowExecutionAlreadyStartedError
sources.summary: Thrown when: conflict=FAIL and running; reuse=REJECT_DUPLICATE and closed; reuse=ALLOW_DUPLICATE_FAILED_ONLY and prior run Completed.

sources.label: Temporal docs — Worker Versioning (Deployments)
sources.summary: Worker Deployment Version = deployment name + Build ID (operator-assigned free-form string). VersioningBehavior.PINNED pins a workflow to its current Build ID; AUTO_UPGRADE moves to latest. Server records versions when first poller arrives. Does NOT introspect registered handlers.

sources.label: TS SDK common/worker-deployments.ts — VersioningBehavior PINNED/AUTO_UPGRADE
sources.summary: PINNED: workflow pinned to current Build ID unless manually moved. AUTO_UPGRADE: workflow moves to latest task-queue version on next task dispatch.

sources.label: TS SDK API — DescribeTaskQueueResponse (pollers, versioningInfo, versionsInfo)
sources.summary: pollers: IPollerInfo[] (includes identity). versioningInfo: routing target. versionsInfo: DEPRECATED, ENHANCED-mode only, per-Build-ID taskReachability. Reachability is eventually-consistent and conservative; reports open/new/closed reachability, NOT handler names.

sources.label: TS SDK API — GetWorkerTaskReachabilityRequest (deprecated)
sources.summary: Deprecated: 'Use DescribeTaskQueue.' Returns whether a Build ID is reachable by open/closed/new workflows. taskReachability is eventually-consistent and takes the conservative side until convergence. Cannot report registered handlers.

sources.label: TS SDK API — DescribeWorkerDeploymentResponse / DescribeWorkerDeploymentVersionRequest
sources.summary: Worker Deployment API (versioning-3). Returns WorkerDeploymentInfo with VersionSummaries + DrainageStatus. Build IDs and deployment names are operator-assigned identifiers; the API tracks routing/drainage, not code-level handler registration.

sources.label: Temporal docs — Workers: Worker Identity
sources.summary: Worker Identity defaults to ${process.pid}@${os.hostname()}; operator-assigned free-form string visible in pollers list and event history. A tracing label, not a code-identity or handler-set proof.

sources.label: TS SDK worker-options.ts — buildId is operator-assigned
sources.summary: buildId: 'A string that should be unique to the exact worker code/binary being executed... Required if useVersioning is true.' It is a CLAIM by the operator, not server-introspected from code.

sources.label: Temporal issue #2860 — RequestCancel on completed returns OK
sources.summary: RequestCancelWorkflowExecution against an already-completed workflow returns OK (no error). Cancel is best-effort by design; docs were corrected to drop the 'fails if completed' claim. Not usable as a 'only-if-still-X' guard.

sources.label: Temporal community: Race between signal handler and workflow completing
sources.summary: Once the workflow function returns the workflow is completed and its activities are cancelled/not retried. Fix: await wf.condition(wf.allHandlersFinished) before return. Confirms single-threaded self-arbiter semantics.

sources.label: Temporal docs — Continue-As-New
sources.summary: CaN completes current execution and atomically starts a new one with same Workflow ID, fresh Event History. 'Workflows that do this are often called Entity Workflows because they represent durable objects.' Bounds history, NOT running-workflow count.

sources.label: Temporal docs — Event History limits
sources.summary: Hard limits: 51,200 Events or 50MB history; >10,000 signals or >2,000 updates terminate the workflow. 'There is no time constraint on how long a Workflow Execution can run.' No per-namespace running-workflow COUNT cap documented.

sources.label: Temporal docs — Entity Workflow design pattern
sources.summary: Official recommendation for one-workflow-per-entity. 'Use entity ID as Workflow ID.' Must use Continue-As-New to prevent unbounded history. 'One Workflow per entity means you should consider costs at scale.' Not a fit for 'entities with only CRUD operations (use a database).'

sources.label: Temporal docs — Entity lifecycle patterns
sources.summary: Entity Workflow + Continue-As-New + Updatable Timer are the official lifecycle patterns. CaN is the prescribed history-bound mechanism; nothing here prescribes completing-then-recreating idle entities.

sources.label: Temporal blog — Managing very long-running Workflows
sources.summary: Entity Workflow = Workflows representing something that potentially lives forever. CaN is the mechanism to run forever. No guidance to hibernate idle entity workflows.

sources.label: Temporal docs — Cloud limits
sources.summary: Cloud limits: 20,000 activity + 20,000 workflow-task pollers per namespace; 2,000 incomplete in-flight commands per workflow execution; 51,200 events / 50MB history; APS/RPS/OPS rate limits. NO documented per-namespace cap on concurrent RUNNING workflow executions.

sources.label: Temporal docs — Cost optimization (Active vs Retained Storage)
sources.summary: Active Storage (open workflows + their histories) is 'significantly more expensive' than Retained Storage. Missing Continue-As-New is the named cost anti-pattern. CaN before long sleeps 'closes the current execution (moving to cheaper Retained Storage) and starts fresh when work resumes.' Closest official analogue to the hibernation proposal — but CaN-based, not complete-and-recreate.

sources.label: Temporal community: How queries on completed workflows work
sources.summary: Queries are answered by a worker replaying the (closed) history using current code — query results reflect the code of whichever worker served the query. Confirms query = point-in-time code-execution probe, not a stored artifact.

sources.label: sdk-core sticky_queues.md — query dispatch via poller
sources.summary: Workers recreate state by replaying history then issue task completion; query tasks are dispatched through the same matching/poller path. Confirms queries execute on a live poller.

subagent_reports.architecture_assessment: Three preconditions gate hibernation. (1) Running-worker signal-set identity has NO native Temporal API: DescribeTaskQueue/Worker-Versioning/Deployments expose operator-assigned Build IDs and eventually-consistent reachability, never the set of registered signal-handler names. A workflow QUERY is a viable point-in-time code-identity probe (queries execute on a live poller with isReplayingHistoryEvents=false) but is sound ONLY under PINNED worker versioning (workflow pinned to one build so query and subsequent signal route to the same code); without versioning it is a racy TOCTOU check. (2) Race-free self-completion IS cheaply satisfiable: a self-completing signal makes the single-threaded workflow the arbiter of its own close; the only residual race (signal arrives during the close window) is handled by server-side UnhandledCommand rollback, and is lossless WHEN a handler exists. Recreate-on-demand is cheap via WorkflowIdReusePolicy.ALLOW_DUPLICATE (default) + signalWithStart. (3) The premise that running-workflow COUNT is the thing to bound is questionable: Temporal has no per-namespace running-count cap, 191 idle workflows is operationally trivial, and the documented cost lever is Active Storage of open histories — which Continue-As-New already bounds and which the official Entity-Workflow + CaN pattern is designed to carry indefinitely. The deeper hibernation risk is silent data loss: a signal sent to a name NO worker build registers is buffered in SDK memory and is SILENTLY DISCARDED when the workflow completes (transient UnhandledCommand during the close race resolves to loss, not stuck); only setDefaultSignalHandler gives visibility. This loss is a real hazard for hibernation specifically because complete-then-recreate widens the window in which the host may emit a signal the (about-to-close / not-yet-recreated) workflow cannot handle.

validation.notes: Research succeeded; no source-access blocker. Caution (not fail) because no precondition is strictly unsatisfiable, but Q1's identity precondition is satisfiable only expensively (requires adopting PINNED worker versioning + an identity query + accepting a TOCTOU window), and Q3 shows the motivating premise (running count = cost driver) is weakly supported by documented limits — the cheaper, officially-blessed lever is Continue-As-New. Two material risks surface for the orchestrator to weigh: (a) silent signal loss on hibernation when the host emits a name no registered handler covers; (b) the identity-prevention check cannot be made lossless without versioning discipline.

tradeoffs: Hibernation (complete + signalWithStart-recreate) reduces Active Storage cost of idle open workflows but introduces a silent-signal-loss window that Continue-As-New does not have (CaN preserves pending signals across the chain).

A query-based running-worker identity probe is cheap to build but is sound only under PINNED worker versioning; adopting versioning is itself a non-trivial operational commitment (Build ID discipline, deployment management, drainage monitoring).

Bounding running-workflow count addresses a metric (count) that Temporal does not limit per-namespace; the real cost lever (Active Storage GB) is already bounded by Continue-As-New, which the codebase appears to already use for terminal completion.

Self-completing signals make close race-free w.r.t. workflow-internal state, but RequestCancel is best-effort and returns OK on already-completed workflows — it cannot serve as a 'complete only if still X' guard, so the design must use signal-driven self-close, not external cancel/terminate.

alternatives_considered.option: Continue-As-New with infrequent inactivity timers (official Entity-Workflow pattern)
alternatives_considered.rationale: Officially blessed for 'workflows that run forever.' Bounds history (the real storage cost), preserves pending signals across the chain (no silent loss), needs no identity probe. Downsides: does NOT reduce running-workflow count, and timers do not survive CaN (must be carried in input).

alternatives_considered.option: Hibernation (complete stale workflows + signalWithStart recreate on demand)
alternatives_considered.rationale: Reduces running count and Active Storage of truly-idle workflows. Costs: silent-signal-loss window (mitigated only by setDefaultSignalHandler + backward-compatible signal set), expensive/unsound identity check without versioning, and recreate-on-demand latency on first touch after idle. Defer until Active-Storage/APS cost evidence justifies the added risk.

alternatives_considered.option: Hybrid: CaN for bounded-history long-life + hibernate only on a true inactivity timeout with default-signal-handler draining
alternatives_considered.rationale: Use CaN as the primary history bound; add hibernation only as an explicit inactivity-timeout transition that first drains via setDefaultSignalHandler (logging any unhandled name) before completing. Minimizes the loss window and makes any divergence observable. Defer until/unless hibernation is committed; then this is the strongest form.

alternatives_considered.option: External database for entity state instead of one-workflow-per-entity
alternatives_considered.rationale: Temporal's own Entity-Workflow doc says CRUD-only entities should use a database. If ADV changes were mostly CRUD with occasional process logic, a DB + short-lived process workflows might be simpler — but this is a larger architectural change outside this change's scope and ADV's durable per-change workflow carries genuine process logic, so rejected for this context.

architecture_judgement.recommendation: Do NOT gate the design on a native running-worker-identity API — none exists. If hibernation is pursued: (1) adopt PINNED worker versioning so the identity probe (a registered query returning handler names) is sound, OR enforce a backward-compatible signal-set invariant (signal names are add-only across versions) so divergence cannot occur and the identity check becomes unnecessary; (2) implement close via a self-completing signal after await wf.condition(wf.allHandlersFinished), never via external RequestCancel/Terminate; (3) install setDefaultSignalHandler that logs every unhandled name BEFORE completing, so any divergence is observable rather than silently lost; (4) recreate with signalWithStart under WorkflowIdReusePolicy.ALLOW_DUPLICATE. Separately, re-examine whether 191 running workflows is a real cost problem — the documented levers (Active Storage, APS) point at Continue-As-New, not at count reduction.

subagent_reports.recommendation: See architecture_judgement.recommendation. Summary: Q1 identity = NOT satisfiable natively, expensively satisfiable via versioned query-probe (recommend the add-only signal-set invariant instead, which dissolves the precondition). Q2 completion race = SATISFIABLE CHEAPLY via self-completing signal + allHandlersFinished + ALLOW_DUPLICATE/signalWithStart. Q3 = the cheaper answer is Continue-As-New (already in use for terminal completion); running-count bounding is solving a weakly-documented problem — verify the actual Active Storage / APS cost before committing to hibernation complexity.
follow_ups: adv_change_show timed out (10s) on first call this session; session-health flagged the active change as possibly unsafe to continue from chat history. Orchestrator should resume decideWorkflowHibernation in a fresh session by changeId before relying on any in-flight context.

Verify the codebase's actual signal-emission surface: enumerate every signal name the host (ADV plugin) sends to change workflows. If that set is add-only across all deployed worker builds, the Q1 identity precondition is dissolved for free and hibernation's data-loss risk collapses to 'only loses signals whose handlers were removed/renamed', which should be a release-gated invariant, not a runtime probe.
Confirm whether ADV workers already use Worker Deployment Versioning (buildId/deploymentName). If not, the query-probe identity check is unsound and must not be relied upon.

Measure the real cost driver before committing: pull Active Storage GB and APS for the ADV namespace. 191 open workflows is far below any documented Cloud limit; the decision should be evidence-led, not count-led.

If hibernation proceeds, add a regression test that signals an unregistered name to a workflow in its close window and asserts the signal is observable via setDefaultSignalHandler (not silently dropped).

sources.label: Temporal continue-as-new design pattern
sources.summary: Authoritative: 'Forgetting to drain Signals before continuing. Any Signals received but not yet processed are lost when Continue-As-New starts a fresh execution.' Continue-as-new does NOT automatically preserve pending signals; author must drain and carry as args.

sources.label: Temporal TS SDK — message passing / allHandlersFinished
sources.summary: Guidance is to wait for allHandlersFinished before continue-as-new; signals processed by handlers, not auto-serialized to next run. Completion and continue-as-new share this drain requirement.

sources.label: Temporal community — TS SDK signals and continueAsNew
sources.summary: Maintainer confirms at high signal rates 'the application has to be remodeled' and signals must be carried manually to the next run. Confirms no automatic carry-over.

sources.label: Temporal TS SDK source — setDefaultSignalHandler
sources.summary: setDefaultSignalHandler calls activator.dispatchBufferedSignals() — dispatch is WITHIN the same run, not a carry to the next run. Confirms unregistered-signal discard is not solved by continue-as-new.

sources.label: Temporal entity-workflow pattern
sources.summary: Entity workflows run for entity lifetime, use continue-as-new for longevity, complete only on entity deletion/terminal. No guidance recommends completing idle live entities to bound running count. Supports design claim #4.

sources.label: Temporal entity loyalty-points guide
sources.summary: 'Unprocessed Signals are preserved' is achieved by the workflow MANUALLY serializing them into state passed to continue_as_new — not automatic SDK behavior. Confirms claim #3 misattributes the mechanism.

sources.label: Temporal control-plane blog (entity workflow)
sources.summary: Entity workflow = durable control-plane record for a resource; continue-as-new prevents unbounded history. Reinforces workflow-lifetime-mirrors-entity-lifetime as canonical.

sources.label: Temporal GitHub issue #2860 — RequestCancel on completed returns OK
sources.summary: Maintainer confirms RequestCancelWorkflowExecution against a completed workflow returns OK; 'cancellation is very much best-effort.' Supports DEC-2.

sources.label: Temporal GitHub issue #952 / api service.proto
sources.summary: Proto doc comment claims NotFoundFailure on completed workflow, but issue #2860 shows actual behavior returns OK. Supports DEC-2 'unusable as guard' conclusion.

sources.summary: Verified: WORKER_BUNDLE_FILES=['worker.js','workflows.js']; generation = SHA-256 over both file hashes+names. Generation equality DOES establish workflows.js byte-equality = registered signal-set equality. DEC-1 proxy claim technically correct.

sources.summary: Verified: BOTH terminal-completion (2281) and continue-as-new (2287) drain via wf.allHandlersFinished; continue-as-new carries a state seed via buildChangeWorkflowContinueAsNewSeed, NOT pending/unregistered signals. Refutes design claim #3 as applied to ADV's own code.

sources.summary: Spec law: production change workflow SHALL remain signal/query based, SHALL NOT reintroduce defineUpdate; regression tests fail on defineUpdate. DEC-2 self-completion-by-signal respects this (C2 satisfied).

subagent_reports.architecture_assessment: The NEGATIVE verdict is architecturally sound and consistent with Temporal's canonical entity-workflow pattern: workflow lifetime mirrors entity lifetime, continue-as-new handles history longevity, completion happens only at entity-terminal. Four of five shape arguments (#1 entity-mirror-correct, #2 cache-vs-mirror regression, #4 no Temporal guidance to complete idle entities, #5 real defect is entity-lifecycle discipline) are well-supported by official Temporal docs and stand independently. DEC-1's bundle-generation proxy is verified correct at the code level for signal-SET equality (worker-bundle-manifest.ts:29,81-89 hashes workflows.js, which carries every wf.setHandler). DEC-2's self-completion-by-signal is the correct single-threaded arbiter pattern, and RequestCancel returning OK on completed workflows is confirmed (temporal #2860). DEC-3/DEC-4/DEC-5 are appropriately scoped. HOWEVER, shape argument #3 contains a load-bearing factual inaccuracy: it asserts continue-as-new 'serializes pending signals into the next run' and is 'strictly safer' on signal grounds. Temporal docs and ADV's own code contradict this — continue-as-new ALSO drops undrained/unregistered signals unless the workflow manually carries them (ADV does not; it carries only a state seed at workflows.ts:2286). The actual architectural difference is liveness (continue-as-new keeps the entity able to receive future signals; completion ends reception), not signal preservation. Must be restated before ADR approval; correction strengthens the design by making #3 consistent with DEC-5.

blockers.finding: Shape argument #3 asserts 'Completion discards signals; continue-as-new preserves them' and 'Continue-as-new serializes pending signals into the next run,' concluding continue-as-new is 'strictly safer than hibernation' on signal-preservation grounds. Factually inaccurate. Temporal's continue-as-new docs state unprocessed signals are LOST on continue-as-new unless manually drained and carried as args; the loyalty guide's 'preserved' wording is achieved by manual state serialization, not automatic SDK behavior; TS SDK continueAsNew() takes args only with no signal auto-carry; setDefaultSignalHandler.dispatchBufferedSignals() is same-run not next-run. ADV's own code (workflows.ts:2285-2288) carries a state seed via buildChangeWorkflowContinueAsNewSeed, not pending/unregistered signals, and BOTH terminal and continue-as-new paths drain only registered handlers via allHandlersFinished. For the DEC-5 unregistered-signal case, completion and continue-as-new BOTH discard. Violates DONT2 (asserts a mechanism guarantees a property — signal preservation — without tracing declaration through consumer to observable effect; the trace refutes it) and undermines the precision AC3/SC2 require of the architectural-shape basis. Does NOT overturn the verdict — arguments #1,#2,#4,#5 independently justify NEGATIVE. Accurate restatement: continue-as-new preserves entity LIVENESS (future signal reception) while completion ends it; neither automatically preserves undrained unregistered signals (exactly why DEC-5/rq-hib04 is verdict-independent).
blockers.in_scope_remediation: Restate shape argument #3 in design.md (the deliverable of this decision-only change, so fully in-scope). Replace the signal-preservation framing with the liveness framing: 'Both completion and continue-as-new drop undrained/unregistered signals; ADV mitigates registered signals via allHandlersFinished in both paths. The architectural difference is that continue-as-new preserves the entity's ability to RECEIVE future signals (keeps the durable mirror alive), while completing a live entity (hibernation) ends reception and requires recreation via signalWithStart. This liveness asymmetry — not a signal-serialization guarantee — is why continue-as-new is the sanctioned longevity mechanism.' Also makes #3 consistent with DEC-5 and removes the false 'strictly safer on signal grounds' premise. No verdict change, no new scope.

source.locator: https://docs.temporal.io/design-patterns/continue-as-new ('Any Signals received but not yet processed are lost when Continue-As-New starts a fresh execution'); https://docs.temporal.io/develop/typescript/workflows/message-passing; plugin/src/temporal/workflows.ts:2285-2288 (continueAsNew carries state seed, not signals)

validation.notes: Verdict (NEGATIVE) is sound and survives correction of claim #3. Spec-law compliance PASS: no existing spec requires a positive hibernation decision; C2 (signal/query-only, no defineUpdate) satisfied by DEC-2's self-completion-by-signal and enforced by advance-delivery spec + workflow-bundle-boundary.test.ts; DEC-4's recording of an unresolved mechanism satisfies C3 (separates established fact from unestablished mechanism) and violates no evidence/verification spec law because it explicitly declines to assert the mechanism. DDC1-DDC5 well-formed and traceable. Revisit trigger measurable (SQL join on history_node bytes x executions_visibility.status=1; DDC5 pins the method; note it is dev-server-sqlite-specific). required_validation_consistency.status = caution. Alternatives disposed: (a) namespace retention/archival orthogonal (closed-history, freelist_count=0 healthy) acceptably implicit; (b) lower continue-as-new threshold correctly disposed; (c) scheduled reaper IS the preferred alternative; (d) multi-namespace split omitted, acceptable for decision-only shape ADR, revisit trigger implicitly covers.

tradeoffs: Recording a contested 5-round decision with full evidence anchors (DEC-1..5, DDC1-5) adds document weight but is justified by DONT1/DONT3's anti-re-litigation objective; a thinner record would invite a seventh round.
Inline ADR (vs docs/adr/) matches ADR-0001/0003 precedent and keeps the decision adjacent to the change, at the cost of discoverability for readers who scan docs/adr/.
Negative verdict accepts bounded growth (71.9MB, 0.8-1.6MB/day) until entity-lifecycle discipline happens; mitigated by a measurable revisit trigger but real if discipline stalls.
DEC-4 leaves orphan mechanism unresolved by design (C3); correct for a decision-only change but means 93.5MB reclamation deferred with no owner-bound timeline.

Revisit-trigger thresholds (500MB / 10MB-day-over-30d) are measurable on the local dev-server sqlite but would need restating for a real Temporal deployment; acceptable since ADV targets the local server topology.

alternatives_considered.option: Namespace-level retention/archival config to bound history
alternatives_considered.rationale: Retention governs CLOSED-workflow history, not running count; design reports retention already healthy (freelist_count=0, zero closed past 24h). Orthogonal to the running-workflow question; not a missed disposal, just not the same problem.

Design's alternatives table disposes it accurately: bounds history not running count, and max observed history is 46% of the current threshold so it would rarely fire. Verified against Temporal entity-pattern guidance.

alternatives_considered.option: Scheduled reaper bringing abandoned entities terminal
alternatives_considered.rationale: This IS the design's preferred alternative (entity-lifecycle discipline, P40 repair). Correctly identified as repairing the owning invariant rather than compensating. Consistent with prior per-session-task-queue reaping precedent (isolateAdvWorkerTaskQueues etc., all terminal).

alternatives_considered.option: Split ADV state across multiple namespaces
alternatives_considered.rationale: Not discussed in the design. Would bound per-namespace running count but adds major cross-namespace query/worker-config complexity and is an implementation-level escape hatch, not a shape decision. The revisit trigger implicitly covers 'if growth becomes unbearable.' Acceptable to omit in a decision-only shape ADR; worth a one-line acknowledgment if a future affirmative revisit occurs (DONT1-adjacent).

architecture_judgement.recommendation: Proceed toward ADR approval AFTER restating shape argument #3. validation.notes: SPEC LAW: rq-changeWorkflowSignalOnly01 (advance-delivery) — NO CONFLICT (DEC-2 delivers hibernation as a self-signal). rq-changeLifecycleState01 (advance-workflow v1.44.0) — FORWARD CONFLICT: current spec defines lifecycleState as exactly three values (open, archived, closed) with sole open-claim authority = AdvLifecycleState='open' AND ExecutionStatus='Running'. A hibernated workflow (ExecutionStatus != Running) would NOT be open-claim authoritative under the current spec; the implementation change MUST amend rq-changeLifecycleState01 to add a 'hibernated' lifecycle state with explicit open-claim semantics. DDC8 acknowledges the code-level enum extension (plugin/src/types/changes.ts:270-303,315-329) but not the spec amendment. rq-workflowVersioning01 applies to the implementation change (hibernation is command-producing), not to this decision-only design. REQUIRED_VALIDATION_CONSISTENCY: status=pass (the validation surface itself is consistent; the blockers are content defects, not tooling gaps). The affirmative verdict is DEFENSIBLE on Arguments 2, 3, 4 and F7 even after Argument 1 is corrected — the reversal is not pure capitulation. Three additional non-blocking concerns: (1) rq-changeLifecycleState01 spec amendment unacknowledged in design; (2) narrower epic-only scope alternative under-considered; (3) DDC2-DDC10 tail (including DDC9 cost-baseline rule and DDC10 disk-persist gate) was truncated and could not be verified — the DDC9 principle ('baseline requires measuring before, not after, a cleanup pass') is sound experimental methodology but the exact wording and applicability could not be checked.

tradeoffs: Hibernation introduces a fourth lifecycle state (not in current rq-changeLifecycleState01 three-state model) requiring spec amendment and explicit representation everywhere workflow existence is consumed (DDC8).

Promoting rq-hib04 to a blocking prerequisite is the correct ordering (hibernation increases completion events, which is when buffered signals are lost per F3) but adds a serialization constraint on the implementation roadmap.

signalWithStart recreation from disk projection preserves resumability (genuine advantage over a naive reaper) but the in-memory workflow state IS lost on completion — resumability depends entirely on the disk projection's correctness (DDC10 gates this).

Argument 1's corrected framing (abandoned-not-deleted entities, not 'pattern assumes termination') is a weaker rhetorical anchor than the original false claim, requiring the affirmative case to lean more heavily on Arguments 2-4.

alternatives_considered.rationale: Epics (40 running, 0 closed, no close path) are 100% affected and represent a pure structural defect. Changes (38% never-terminal per invalidated measurement) have an existing archive close path and the issue is human discipline, not missing capability. An epic-only hibernation would deliver the structural benefit at materially lower risk: no new lifecycle state for the common case, no DDC8 ambiguity for changes, simpler spec amendment. The design mentions 'epic hibernation may need to precede change hibernation' (DEC-3) but does not analyze epic-ONLY as an alternative to broad hibernation. This is the simplest mechanism that addresses the strongest case (P19, P29).

The design's distinction is real but narrower than framed. Force-termination destroys in-memory state AND buffered signals (F4: no Workflow Task scheduled, so no cleanup runs). Hibernation (project-to-disk-then-complete via the existing terminal path at workflows.ts:2260-2283) preserves resumability via disk projection. However, a reaper COULD also project state before terminating — the real distinction is that hibernation establishes structural recreation semantics (signalWithStart + WorkflowIdReusePolicy.ALLOW_DUPLICATE + DDC10 disk-persist gate), while a reaper does not. Worth revisiting as a complement for genuinely dead entities (the design notes this).

alternatives_considered.option: Maintain NEGATIVE verdict, address epics via addEpicClosePath only
alternatives_considered.rationale: If epics are the only structural defect (changes have an archive path), then adding an epic close path (already tracked as addEpicClosePath) plus rq-hib04 standalone hardening could address the structural gap without introducing a new lifecycle state. This avoids the spec conflict (rq-changeLifecycleState01) and the DDC8 ambiguity. The design rejects this implicitly by treating addEpicClosePath as 'complementary to hibernation rather than an alternative.' But if epic close path + automatic staleness-based change archiving were combined, the boundedness goal could be met without hibernation. This alternative deserves explicit comparison.

architecture_judgement.recommendation: Proceed toward design-gate approval CONDITIONAL on repairing two blockers: (1) reframe Argument 1 to accurately represent Temporal's entity-workflow documentation — the pattern contemplates indefinite lifetime via continue-as-new and recommends an explicit deletion signal; ADV's gap is abandoned-not-deleted entities and missing epic close path, NOT a pattern-level termination assumption; (2) rewrite the stale Executive Summary to match the affirmative verdict with architectural-shape basis. documents.proposal:
## Problem

191 running Temporal workflows, growing monotonically with lifetime change count. Closing changes does not reclaim them. ADV needs a lifecycle state that lets a stale change's workflow complete and be recreated on demand.

## Starting position — what five review rounds already settled

This change starts from a verified position rather than from zero. The following are **established** and should not be re-litigated without new evidence:

**Ruled out as mechanisms:**
- *In-workflow durable signal queue.* Temporal workflow code cannot perform filesystem or network I/O; a handler cannot persist a `queuedSignals[]` to disk. Any design that "persists from a handler" is invalid by construction.
- *`continueAsNew` as the bounding mechanism.* Bounds history size, not running count.
- *Auto-archive, creation ceiling, shared workflow, lazy-spawn.* Each rejected with reasons recorded in the parent change's design.md.
- *`evaluateWorkerDeploymentReadiness` as a version-skew gate.* It governs Worker Versioning readiness (build IDs, ramping, drainage), has no signal/handler parity concept, and records ADV's current `singleton_replace_in_place` topology as explicitly not-ready.
- *`dualWriteAfterMutation` as a durability basis.* It is labeled "Best-effort by design: this is a cache-refresh path" (`plugin/src/storage/store-temporal/index.ts:411`) and skips the disk write on non-`confirmed` readback (`:399`), empty readback (`:405`), or poisoned workflow (`:366`) — precisely the degraded conditions under which hibernation would fire.
- *`verifyDeployedBuildIdentity` alone as a parity gate.* It inspects the bundle on disk, not the code a long-lived worker process is executing.

**Established as sound:**
- The completion path already exists and already drains handlers correctly: `plugin/src/temporal/workflows.ts:2221-2240` completes on terminal status after `await wf.condition(wf.allHandlersFinished)`. Hibernation is a new trigger on that path, not new machinery.
- All `wf.setHandler` calls register synchronously before the first await (`:1703-2209` vs `:2221`), so within one worker build no known-name signal is buffered-without-handler at hibernation time.
- `assertDurablePersist` / `DiskPersistOutcome` (`plugin/src/storage/store-temporal/disk-persist.ts:31,44`) is the real durability gate. Only a `persisted` outcome is meaningful for hibernation; `skipped` means `archived` and signals a terminal race, not a benign no-op.
- The operation ledger (`plugin/src/temporal/change-state.ts:376-510`) dedupes retried signals by `operation_id`, bounded to 1000 entries, making resume-then-retry safe for post-completion signal races.
- `plugin/src/temporal/recovery-classification.ts:104-111,138` already classifies the already-completed / not-running error family (`missing_workflow`) that a post-completion signal produces.

---

# Discovery Findings (2026-08-04)

Discovery set out to firm the two preconditions the proposal named as blocking. It resolved both — and in doing so measured the motivating premise, which does not hold as stated.

**Headline: the two "blocking" preconditions are cheap or already solved. The premise they were blocking is the thing that failed verification.**

## Finding 1 — Precondition 1 (running-worker identity) is ALREADY SOLVED in this repo

The proposal states: *"No running-worker identity report exists today… This is new work whose cost has not been estimated."*

**This is incorrect.** A running-worker identity mechanism exists, is liveness-gated, and is actively self-healing. Full trace (declaration → sole writer → consumer → observable effect, per P38):

| Link | Anchor | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| Generation defined | `plugin/src/temporal/worker-bundle-manifest.ts:29,81-89` | `generation` = SHA-256 over `worker.js` **+ `workflows.js`** file hashes with names. `workflows.js` is the file carrying every `wf.setHandler` registration — so the generation is a precise proxy for "which signal set does this code register". |
| Declared on the lock | `plugin/src/temporal/worker-lock.ts:33,87-89` | `bundle_generation` written at acquire. |
| Sole post-acquire writer | `plugin/src/temporal/worker-heartbeat.ts:99-117,169-176` | `renewLockNow` persists `bundle_generation` + `last_heartbeat` in one atomic tmp+rename, every beat (10s). Deliberately the only writer — a second RMW path would race and lose updates. |
| Drift detection | `plugin/src/temporal/worker-roll.ts:133-155` | Every beat compares on-disk manifest generation against the generation the running child was spawned with (tracked in-memory, lock value as fallback). Owner-pid gated. |
| Drift response | `plugin/src/temporal/worker-roll.ts:197-216` | On drift → `restartChild()` (graceful SIGTERM drain, readiness-gated) → record new generation → stamp lock. Single-flight latched. |
| Safety gate | `plugin/src/temporal/worker-roll.ts:160-195` | Refuses to roll onto a candidate bundle that fails replay verification unless `ADV_FORCE_DEPLOY=1`. |
| Freshness bound | `worker-lock.ts:7,210-220` | 60s stale-heartbeat grace; pid liveness probe. |

**Consequence.** "Is the running worker executing the deployed workflow code?" is answerable now, cheaply, from local state: `in-memory/lock bundle_generation == on-disk manifest generation` AND heartbeat fresh AND owner pid alive. No new Temporal API, no worker versioning adoption, no query-probe. The proposal's rejection of `verifyDeployedBuildIdentity` was correct about that function — but concluded no mechanism exists, missing the three modules that supply the other half (binding *running child* to *generation*).

This is a sixth instance of the failure mode the problem statement names — but inverted: the design **under**-credited an existing mechanism instead of over-crediting one.

**Independent corroboration (external research):** Temporal offers **no** native API that reports a running worker's registered handler set. `DescribeTaskQueue` pollers expose only an operator-supplied `identity` string; `versionsInfo` / `GetWorkerTaskReachability` / `DescribeWorkerDeployment` expose Build IDs and reachability, and `buildId` is itself an operator-assigned claim, not server-introspected from code. `DescribeWorker` does not exist. A workflow **query** could serve as a probe (queries are served by a live worker executing real code, non-replaying), but it is sound only under `VersioningBehavior.PINNED` — otherwise any polling build may answer, giving a TOCTOU. **ADV's bundle-generation mechanism is strictly cheaper and already deployed.**

## Finding 2 — Precondition 2 (hibernation/terminal race) is cheap

Sourced from Temporal docs/SDK:

- **Self-completing signal is the correct primitive.** The workflow is the single-threaded arbiter of its own state, so "complete only if still non-terminal" is decided inside the workflow with no external race. (`docs.temporal.io/handling-messages`)
- **External cancel/terminate is wrong.** `RequestCancelWorkflowExecution` is best-effort and returns OK against an already-completed workflow — it cannot serve as a guard. (`temporalio/temporal#2860`)
- **The close-window race is lossless when a handler exists.** A signal arriving during the final workflow task fails the WFT with `UNHANDLED_COMMAND`, rolls back, and reprocesses. (`failed_cause.proto`)
- **Recreation works.** `WorkflowIdReusePolicy.ALLOW_DUPLICATE` (the default) permits starting the same workflow id after close; `signalWithStart` against a completed id starts a new run and delivers the signal. That *is* the recreate-on-demand mechanism. ADV sets no explicit reuse/conflict policy today (`plugin/src/temporal/operations.ts:947-967`), so the permissive default already applies.

**Residual hazard, and it is real:** a signal sent for a name the running worker does **not** register is buffered in SDK memory and **silently discarded** when the workflow completes — no error, no warning. Hibernation widens that window. Mitigation is cheap and independent: install `setDefaultSignalHandler` to log unhandled signal names, and hold an add-only invariant on the signal set across deployed builds.

## Finding 3 — The motivating premise does not survive measurement

Measured directly against the live server (`temporal` CLI 1.7.2 / Server 1.31.1, local dev server, SQLite, `default` namespace, 24h retention):

| Claim | Measured | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| 191 running workflows | **189** — 149 `adv/change/`, 40 `adv/epic/`, 15 projects, zero non-ADV | Substantially correct |
| Running count is costing something | Server **531 MB RSS / 7.9% CPU**. Task queue backlog **0**, add rate **0** — the 189 are idle, not working | **Not supported** |
| Read latency pain from count | `workflow count` ~60ms · `list --limit 200` ~125ms · `describe` ~65ms · `cluster health` ~58ms | **Not supported** |
| Session's 8s Temporal timeouts are caused by workflow count | `TEMPORAL_READ_DEADLINE_BUDGET_MS = 8_000` (`plugin/src/temporal/retry-wrapper.ts:203`) is a **per-request aggregate** wall-clock budget covering all retries/backoff for one read. Independent of running-workflow count. | **Refuted — different root cause** |
| `continueAsNew` is irrelevant because it bounds history not count | True as stated, but: threshold is 5000 events (`contracts.ts:953`); **max observed history across all 149 running changes is 2320 (46%)**; `StartTime == OriginalStartTime` on every sampled workflow — **no ADV workflow has ever continued-as-new** | Mechanism exists, never yet exercised |

**The one real cost slope:** the SQLite DB is **410 MB, of which `history_node` is 380 MB (93%)**, growing **~500 MB/day**. Namespace retention is 24h — but **retention only reclaims CLOSED workflows.** 189 never-closing workflows hold their history permanently. *That* is the defensible cost argument for hibernation, and it is a different argument from the one the proposal makes. It is a slope, not a wall: the host has 47 GB available and loadavg is not workflow-bound.

## Finding 4 — Root cause is portfolio hygiene, not Temporal lifecycle (P40)

Age distribution of the 149 running change workflows: **112 are ≥ 1 week old**; only 9 are < 1 day. Cross-referencing the change inventory (245 total): the long tail is `status: draft` changes parked for weeks at `phase: release` or `phase: proposal` — created, worked, and abandoned without ever reaching `archived` or `closed`.

Termination is **not** broken: the server holds **196 Terminated + 26 Completed** workflows. The close path works. The growth driver is that **changes are never brought to a terminal state**, so their workflows correctly stay running.

Per P40 (root-cause-first): hibernation is a *compensating* mechanism for accumulation whose owning mechanism — bringing changes to terminal state — is under-exercised, not defective. ADV already ships the owning surface (`/adv-triage`, the `adv-cleanup` skill, `adv_change_close`, `adv_change_archive`). Running a portfolio sweep would reclaim the same resource with no new machinery, no new lifecycle state, and no silent-signal-loss hazard.

Hibernation remains defensible as *defense-in-depth* for the residual case (a project legitimately holding many long-lived open changes) — but P40 permits defense-in-depth only for an independently stated failure mode that already has a primary control. The primary control here has not been exercised.

Inventory complete: 245 changes across 5 pages, `hydrationStats.omitted: 0` throughout. **No active change conflicts with this one.** All 33 workflow-lifecycle-adjacent changes are `closed` or `archived`.

- `autoRollStaleWorkerBundle` (archived, 5/5) — **built the worker-roll drift/self-heal machinery that dissolves precondition 1**

- One Temporal workflow per change (`adv/change/{projectId}/{changeId}`) + per epic. Completes only on `archived`/`closed`, or continues-as-new at 5000 events.
- 189 running / 420 total; 15 projects; 410 MB SQLite (93% history).
- Worker: out-of-process Node child (`worker-multi.ts:374-378`), lock-owned, heartbeat 10s, self-rolls on bundle drift.

## Edge Cases

**Gap A — hibernation trigger fires against a change that is concurrently going terminal**
1. Change archived between candidate selection and precondition evaluation → self-completing signal observes `archived` first and completes on the normal terminal path; hibernation is a no-op. Safe by construction.
2. `assertDurablePersist` returns `skipped` — which means `archived`, not a benign no-op. Treating `skipped` as success would hibernate a change mid-archive.

**Gap B — signal arrives for a hibernated (completed) workflow**
1. Known signal name, workflow completed → `signalWithStart` under `ALLOW_DUPLICATE` recreates and delivers. Operation ledger dedupes if the host retries. Safe.
2. Signal name the *running* build does not register → buffered in SDK memory, **silently discarded on completion**. No error surface today. This is the one genuinely unsafe path, and it exists independently of hibernation — hibernation only widens the window.

**Gap C — recreation from disk projection**
1. Disk projection is stale relative to the completed workflow's final state (`dualWriteAfterMutation` skipped) → recreated workflow seeds from stale state, silently losing the delta.
2. Disk projection missing entirely → recreation has no seed; must fail typed rather than create an empty workflow.

**Gap D — worker generation drift at hibernation time**
1. Deploy lands between drift check and hibernation signal → next beat (≤10s) rolls the worker; hibernation must re-verify rather than trust a stale check.
2. Worker lock heartbeat stale (>60s) or owner pid dead → running-generation claim is unfounded; hibernation must suppress, not assume.

## Open Design Questions

**Q1 — Should hibernation be built at all?**
- *Trust model:* **user-only.** This is a cost/benefit judgment about acceptable resource growth, not a technical question.
- *Blast radius:* Building it adds a lifecycle state, a trigger, a recreation path, and a silent-signal-loss surface, for a benefit measured at ~120 MB of currently-unreclaimable history growing ~500 MB/day gross on a host with 47 GB free. Not building it leaves the slope in place, mitigated by portfolio hygiene.
- *Alternatives:* (a) portfolio sweep only — bring stale changes terminal via existing tooling; (b) hibernation as designed; (c) sweep now + revisit hibernation if the slope persists after the tail is cleared.

**Q2 — If built, what is the running-worker precondition?** *(agent-resolvable, resolved)*
- *Trust model:* agent. **Resolved:** compare lock/in-memory `bundle_generation` to on-disk manifest generation, gated on heartbeat freshness (60s) and owner-pid liveness. No new mechanism. Rejected: Temporal worker versioning (`PINNED`) + query-probe — strictly more expensive, requires adopting a versioning topology the repo has already recorded as not-ready.

**Q3 — If built, how does completion get triggered?** *(agent-resolvable, resolved)*
- *Trust model:* agent. **Resolved:** a self-completing signal handled inside the workflow, releasing the existing `wf.condition` at `workflows.ts:2221` after `allHandlersFinished`. Rejected: client-side `terminate` (destroys handler drain) and `RequestCancelWorkflow` (best-effort, returns OK against completed workflows — cannot guard).

**Q4 — Should `setDefaultSignalHandler` be installed regardless of the hibernation decision?**
- *Trust model:* joint. Silent signal discard is a live hazard today, independent of hibernation. Cheap, additive, purely observability. Recommend yes either way.

## Draft Spec Deltas

Contingent on Q1 resolving affirmative. If Q1 resolves "no build", only `rq-hib04` survives as a standalone hardening delta.

- **rq-hib01 — Hibernation precondition is bundle-generation parity.** Given a hibernation candidate, when preconditions are evaluated, then hibernation proceeds only if the worker lock's `bundle_generation` equals the on-disk manifest generation, the heartbeat is within its grace window, and the owner pid is alive; otherwise hibernation is suppressed and the reason recorded.
- **rq-hib02 — Hibernation completes via self-signal, never external termination.** Given a change selected for hibernation, when hibernation is triggered, then it is delivered as a signal the workflow handles itself, completing after `wf.condition(wf.allHandlersFinished)`; external `terminate`/`cancel` must not be used.
- **rq-hib03 — Recreation is durability-gated.** Given a signal for a hibernated change, when the host recreates the workflow, then the seed derives from a disk projection whose last write was a `persisted` `DiskPersistOutcome`; a `skipped` or `failed` outcome must fail typed rather than seed from unverified state.
- **rq-hib04 — Unhandled signal names are observable.** Given a signal for a name the running workflow build does not register, when it is received, then a default signal handler records the name and change id; silent discard must not be the only outcome. *(Standalone value — survives a "no build" decision.)*
- **rq-hib05 — Hibernated changes remain visible.** Given a hibernated change, when `adv_change_list` is called with default arguments, then the change appears with a hibernation marker; it must not require an opt-in filter.

## Related Pattern Scan

Pattern class: *"long-lived resource per entity, entity count unbounded, no lifecycle terminator."*

- **`adv/epic/` workflows — same pattern, same defect.** 40 running, 40 total, **zero ever closed**. Epics have the identical continue-as-new/terminal structure (`workflows.ts:2494-2522`). Any hibernation decision applies to epics too; a portfolio sweep does not, since epics have no equivalent close path in routine use.
- **Per-session task queues** — `advance-{projectId}-{sessionId}`. Previously accumulated; already addressed by `isolateAdvWorkerTaskQueues`, `adoptOrphanedSessionQueues`, `autoAdoptOrphanSessionQueues`, `reapOrphanAdvWorkers` (all terminal). Precedent: ADV has solved this exact pattern class before, by reaping rather than hibernating.
- **Worker processes** — 3 concurrent workers measured at ~3 GB RSS combined, ~6× the Temporal server's own 531 MB. Not in scope, but worth noting the resource conversation is dominated by workers, not workflows.

## Completeness Verification

**Problem-completeness — was the full problem identified, or only a symptom?** *Confidence: high.* The proposal identified a symptom (running count) and attributed it to a missing lifecycle state. Measurement shows the count is real but harmless, the close path works, and the actual driver is 112 abandoned changes ≥1 week old. The full problem is portfolio accumulation; running-workflow count is its shadow. Epic workflows (40, never closed) were surfaced as an in-scope parallel surface.

**Solution-scope — is the full intended solution scoped?** *Confidence: high.* The proposal scoped one mechanism (hibernation). Discovery surfaced two others addressing the same cost: portfolio sweep (existing tooling, no new machinery) and `setDefaultSignalHandler` (independent hazard). Both are now explicit options rather than silent omissions.

**Sole-entry claim:** none relied upon. The change makes no single-chokepoint claim for a cross-cutting operation; the completion path at `workflows.ts:2221-2240` is a single site but is a *local* structural fact, verified by direct read, not a cross-cutting sole-entry assertion. No broad surface scan required. **Status: not applicable — no blocking claim.**

**Secondary-surface dispositions:**
- **Epic workflows (40 running, never closed)** — *unresolved user-facing scope question.* Carried to the question loop.
- **Per-session task queue accumulation** — *out of scope with rationale:* already solved by four terminal changes.
- **Worker process memory (~3 GB across 3 workers)** — *out of scope with rationale:* distinct resource, distinct owner, no interaction with workflow lifecycle.
- **Read-path 8s deadline** — *out of scope with rationale:* Finding 3 attributes it to a per-request aggregate budget, independent of workflow count; owned by `fixHealthViewTimeoutHealth` / `fixChangeReadTimeouts` / `fixTemporalReadDiagnosis`.

**Reproduction finding classification (rq-acWarrant01):**

| Finding | Classification | May seed a must-work criterion? |
|---|---|---|
| "191 running workflows, growing monotonically" | `broken_capability` (measured 189; growth confirmed; unreclaimable-history slope real) | Yes |
| "Closing changes does not reclaim them" | **`unverified`** — 196 Terminated + 26 Completed exist on the server; the close path demonstrably terminates workflows. The original observation is unexplained and was not reproduced. | **No** |
| "Hibernation requires a new running-worker identity report" | **`unwarranted_operation`** — the capability exists (Finding 1) | **No** |
| "Session Temporal timeouts evidence workflow-count pressure" | **`unverified`** → reclassified: per-request read budget, unrelated to count | **No** |

## LBP Check

**Long-term best practice does not favor hibernation as proposed.**

Temporal's official Entity Workflow guidance (`docs.temporal.io/design-patterns/entity-workflow`, `entity-lifecycle-patterns`) blesses one-workflow-per-entity keyed by entity id, and prescribes **continue-as-new** — not complete-and-recreate — for longevity. Crucially, continue-as-new **preserves pending signals** across the chain, whereas completion **discards** them. There is no official guidance recommending hibernation of idle entity workflows.

Temporal documents **no per-namespace limit on concurrent running workflows** (Cloud limits cover pollers, in-flight commands, history size/event count, and rate — not count). The documented cost lever is **Active Storage**, and the named anti-pattern is *missing* continue-as-new. ADV's continue-as-new exists and has never fired (max history 46% of threshold).

**External-solution check (gated: ecosystem unknown present).** Ran against Temporal official docs, `sdk-typescript`/`sdk-core` source, and community threads. No third-party tool or service addresses this; the decision is entirely internal. No `docs/*-prep.md` pack existed to cite; one is not warranted for a decision this narrow.

**Where LBP does point:** P40 root-cause-first. Exercise the owning mechanism (bring changes terminal) before adding a compensating one. ADV has already solved this exact pattern class by reaping rather than hibernating (session task queues).

## Recommended Objectives

1. **Decide, on measured evidence, whether ADV should adopt a hibernation lifecycle state** — recording the decision, its rationale, and its alternatives as an ADR (ADR-002, inherited from the parent change).
2. **Record the two preconditions as resolved**, so no future round re-litigates them: bundle-generation parity answers running-worker identity; the self-completing signal answers the terminal race.
3. **Dispose of the silent-signal-discard hazard explicitly** — it is independent of the hibernation decision and currently unmitigated.
4. **Resolve whether epic workflows share the decision's scope** (40 running, none ever closed).

## AMBIGUITY ANALYSIS

| S1 | **HIGH** | S | No threshold defines what benefit would justify hibernation's complexity. The proposal asks "does hibernation reclaim enough in practice to be worth its complexity?" but sets no bar, so no measurement can settle it. Discovery measured the cost; the decision rule is still missing. |
| B1 | MEDIUM | B | Epic workflows (40 running, never closed) are not mentioned anywhere in proposal scope, yet share the identical lifecycle structure. In or out? |
| F1 | MEDIUM | F | "Configurable by staleness-days OR active-change-count ceiling" presupposes an affirmative decision. If the decision is negative, this settled scope is void. |
| M1 | MEDIUM | M | The claim "closing 74 changes did not reduce the running count" is unexplained and contradicted by 196 Terminated workflows on the server. Root cause never established. |
| S2 | LOW | S | Success criteria for a decision-only change are undefined — is success "a correct decision" or "a decision that says yes"? |

**Evidence quotes:**
- S1 — *"A third, softer question: if the running-worker precondition suppresses hibernation whenever a deployment is stale or a worker unrestarted, does hibernation reclaim enough in practice to be worth its complexity? That is a real tradeoff, not a formality."*
- B1 — `(no epic scope section)`

- S2 — `(no success criteria section)`

**Coverage: B:P F:C S:P M:P**

**Trigger evaluation:** 0 CRITICAL, 1 HIGH → **advisory, not blocking.** Advisory logged: S1 HIGH — no decision rule defined for "worth it". S1 is resolved by the question loop below, which is where a user-only cost/benefit judgment belongs; it is not a proposal-text ambiguity requiring `/adv-clarify`.

## Discovery Opportunity Scout

**Scout: skipped** — discovery already ran a dedicated `adv-researcher` external-evidence pass (Temporal official docs, `sdk-typescript`/`sdk-core` source, community threads, Cloud limits, entity-workflow guidance) plus a full operational measurement pass against the live server. A third bounded scout pass over the same surface has no remaining opportunity yield.
documents.problemStatement:
ADV accumulates Temporal workflows without bound. Observed 2026-08-04: 191 running workflows across 15 projects, and closing 74 changes did not reduce the running count. There is no mechanism to reclaim Temporal resources from stale changes.

`continueAsNew` does not solve this — it starts a fresh run to bound accumulated HISTORY size, but the workflow keeps running. Bounding *running count* requires the workflow to complete and be recreated on demand.

## Why this is a separate change

This was Decision 2 of `resolveAdvPersistenceRecovery`. It was split out on 2026-08-04 after five independent structural review rounds, each of which found a different foundation assumption that did not survive verification. Decisions 1 and 3 of that change passed clean in all five rounds; every blocker was here.

The repeated failure mode was specific and worth naming: the design kept asserting *"this existing ADV mechanism already guarantees X"* where the mechanism did not. That happened three rounds in a row against three different mechanisms. The conclusion is not that hibernation is wrong — it is that hibernation's preconditions were never firmed at discovery, so design kept reaching for whatever looked adjacent.

> **Lineage.** Fast-follow of `resolveAdvPersistenceRecovery` (status `archived`). Carries that ADR's Decision 2 — pre-split AC2, AC5, C1, C5, C6, DONT4, Objective 2, DDC1/2/5/6/7, and ADR-002 — split out on 2026-08-04 after five structural review rounds. > **Decision criterion (user, 2026-08-04).** Reframed from cost to correctness: *"The slope is less relevant than what is best practice and best shape for temporal and our use."* Architectural shape decides; cost is context only.

> **AC3 amendment (user, 2026-08-05).** AC3's original wording asserted the cost measurements as fact in its Given clause. A reviewer ruled it UNSATISFIABLE-AS-WRITTEN once those measurements were established as invalid. Amended below on user direction to carry the true finding — the measurement omitted the cleanup performed immediately before sampling — rather than being softened into a generic hedge. ## Objectives

1. Decide, on architectural-shape grounds, whether ADV should adopt a workflow hibernation lifecycle state — recorded as ADR-002 with rationale, alternatives, and consequences.
2. Record both blocking preconditions as resolved, with evidence anchors, so no further review round re-litigates them.
3. Decide the disposition of the orphan history pool, separating established fact from unresolved mechanism.
4. Cover epic workflows under the same verdict, and record the absence of a routine epic close path.
5. Dispose of the silent-signal-discard hazard, which is independent of the hibernation verdict.

## Success Criteria

1. The ADR records a decision for every open question with rationale, alternatives, and consequences, so a further review round does not re-litigate resolved ground.
2. The hibernation verdict is justified on architectural-shape grounds against Temporal's documented entity-workflow guidance, with cost treated as context rather than as the deciding factor.
3. Every assumption that discovery or later review overturned is recorded with its evidence anchor.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Given the proposal asserts no running-worker identity report exists and its cost is unestimated, when the ADR is written, then it records that assertion as refuted and names bundle-generation parity (`plugin/src/temporal/worker-bundle-manifest.ts:29`, `plugin/src/temporal/worker-heartbeat.ts:99-117`, `plugin/src/temporal/worker-roll.ts:133-216`) as the resolved mechanism.
2. Given the hibernation and terminal race was unresolved, when the ADR is written, then it records self-completion by signal as the resolution and records external cancel or terminate as unusable because RequestCancelWorkflowExecution returns OK against an already-completed workflow.
3. Given the 71.9 MB unreclaimable, 0.8 to 1.6 MB per day, and 38 percent never-terminal figures were sampled immediately after a manual cleanup pass and therefore omit that cleanup as a variable, when the ADR records its hibernation verdict, then the verdict's stated basis is architectural shape and those figures are recorded as invalid for steady-state reasoning with the omitted cleanup variable named.
4. Given 40 epic workflows are running and none has ever closed, when the ADR is written, then epic workflows are covered by the same verdict and the absence of a routine epic close path is recorded as a distinct finding.
5. Given the orphan history pool of roughly 93.5 MB across 20 workflows, when the ADR records it, then it separates established fact (history scanner healthy, worker.historyScannerEnabled defaults true, ADV calls only terminate and never delete or reset) from unestablished mechanism (what produces orphans and whether the set is still growing), and states the latter as unresolved.
6. Given signals for unregistered names are discarded when a workflow completes, when the ADR is written, then rq-hib04 is recorded with its relationship to the verdict stated explicitly, including any ordering constraint the verdict creates.
7. Evidence: sourced Temporal lifecycle findings captured at `~/.config/opencode/skills/agent-temporal-lifecycle/SKILL.md` verified by file existence and by source-URL citation for each external claim.

## Constraints

1. Must not implement hibernation, orphan reclamation, or setDefaultSignalHandler in this change, because it is decision-only per the parent change.
2. Must preserve the signal and query only workflow surface, with no defineUpdate in workflow-reachable code.
3. Must not present the orphan root cause as established, and must not run any destructive Temporal or SQLite command against live state.
4. Must obtain ADR approval at the design gate before any downstream implementation begins.

## Avoidances

1. Do not re-litigate the ruled-out mechanisms without new evidence.
2. Do not assert that an existing mechanism guarantees a property without tracing declaration through consumer to observable effect.
3. Do not defer the decision by spawning more per-symptom tickets.

## Out of Scope

1. The read-path 8s deadline in `plugin/src/temporal/retry-wrapper.ts:203`, owned by fixHealthViewTimeoutHealth, fixChangeReadTimeouts, and fixTemporalReadDiagnosis.
2. Worker process memory of roughly 3 GB across 3 workers.
3. Per-session task-queue accumulation, already solved by four terminal changes.
4. Implementing any reclamation of orphaned history.

## Preview Applicability

`visual_surface: false` — internal ADV/Temporal architecture, no browser-visible surface.
`preview_expectation`: `exact_route_required: not_applicable`, `data_state_expectation: not_applicable`, `viewport_expectation: not_applicable`.
Rationale: the deliverable is an ADR artifact plus a skill file; no rendered output exists.

## Decisions

### User Decisions

1. **Decision criterion is architectural shape, not cost.** Cost measurements are context and, as it turned out, the refutation of the proposal's own premise. They do not decide the verdict.
2. **Epic workflows are in scope, under the same verdict.** 40 running, zero ever closed.
3. **The silent-signal-discard hazard is addressed regardless of the verdict.** Carried as rq-hib04.
4. **The orphan history pool is in this change's scope** for recording, not for reclamation.
5. **Capture the Temporal lifecycle research as a skill.**
6. **Verdict reversed to AFFIRMATIVE (2026-08-05).** The user rejected the earlier NEGATIVE verdict on two grounds, both sustained: the cost measurement was invalid because it was sampled after a manual cleanup pass, and the P40 argument was inverted because the "discipline" it relied on is recurring manual human effort, which makes automation the repair rather than a compensation.
7. **AC3 amended (2026-08-05).** Rewritten to state that the figures omitted the cleanup-prior-to-measurement variable, rather than asserting them as fact. The user directed that the criterion carry the true information rather than a generic validity hedge.

### Agent Decisions (LBP)

1. **Running-worker identity — resolved as bundle-generation parity.** Compare the worker lock's `bundle_generation` against the on-disk manifest generation, gated on heartbeat freshness and owner-pid liveness. The generation is SHA-256 over `worker.js` and `workflows.js`; `workflows.js` carries every `wf.setHandler`, so equality is a sound proxy for the registered signal set. Rejected: Worker Versioning plus a query-probe (more expensive, not-ready topology). Native worker introspection is insufficient rather than absent — `DescribeWorker`, `ListWorkers` and `RecordWorkerHeartbeat` exist but expose only identity, task queue, SDK name and version, host and process, poller and slot statistics, and resource usage.
2. **Terminal race — resolved as self-completion by signal.** The workflow is the single-threaded arbiter of its own state. External RequestCancelWorkflowExecution is unusable because it returns OK against an already-completed workflow. External terminate is wrong because no Workflow Task is scheduled, so no cleanup runs. This is also the shape Temporal's entity-workflow guidance prescribes for ending an entity workflow.
3. **Orphan root cause deliberately left unresolved.** Two measurement passes used incompatible population predicates and disagreed by roughly 50x. Neither number is adopted.

## Deferred Questions

None.

## Sign-Off

User approved the original criteria at the Phase 4.5.1 inline checkpoint on 2026-08-04. AC3 amended on 2026-08-05 under explicit user direction after a reviewer ruled the original wording unsatisfiable; discovery was re-entered to make the amendment because no contract-amend tool exists. AC6 was also broadened at the same time from "standalone hardening whose value does not depend on the verdict" to requiring the relationship and any ordering constraint be stated explicitly, since the affirmative verdict makes rq-hib04 a blocking prerequisite.

# Design — Workflow Hibernation Lifecycle (ADR-002)

> **Decision-only change.** C1 forbids implementation here. This design *is* the deliverable.

> **Revision history.** v1 NEGATIVE, resting on a cost measurement taken after a manual cleanup pass
> and on an inverted P40 argument (Assumptions 7, 8). v2 reversed to AFFIRMATIVE but justified it
> with a false claim about Temporal's entity-workflow pattern (Assumption 9). v3 removed that claim.
> v4 — this version — names the omitted measurement variable explicitly and restores DEC-5's
> alternatives, both per reviewer findings.

## Architecture Overview

ADV runs one Temporal workflow per change and per epic — the **entity workflow** pattern.

```
entity created ─────────────▶ workflow started (adv/change/<projectId>/<changeId>)
      │                              │
      │  signals (gate, task, …)     │  history grows
      ▼                              ▼
entity terminal ──────────────▶ wf.condition ─▶ project ─▶ drain ─▶ return
      │                                                              │
      │  entity alive but inactive                                   │
      ▼                                                              │
  hibernate signal ─────────▶ same terminal path ─▶ complete         │
      │                                                              │
      │  next signal for this change                                 │
      ▼                                                              │
  signalWithStart ─────────▶ new run, seeded from disk projection    │
                                                                     │
      └────────────── retention (24h) reclaims history ◀─────────────┘
```

## Overturned Assumptions

| # | Assumption as stated | Status | Evidence anchor |
|---|---|---|---|
